answer: A per-identity registration stake is the mechanism. To act as an independent agent, an operator must lock a bond worth far more than one fake signup, and the protocol slashes it on proof of shared control. Ten thousand Sybil identities therefore require ten thousand staked bonds, so cost scales linearly while the attacker's expected loss rises faster once any member is traced. Identity spam becomes a balance-sheet problem, not a free one, and the seized bridge between attestation and payout plus per-attempt timber and copper fees make each blind trial costly.
